hero.alt: Yellow wild flowers and fynbos running down to the Atlantic near Paternoster
hero.body: White cottages, fishing boats on the beach, protected coast and some of the best food on the West Coast — all a short walk from the door.

intro.title:
Whitewashed
*and wind-swept*
intro.lede: Paternoster is one of the oldest fishing villages on South Africa’s West Coast. Its white houses will remind you of a Greek island; its beaches, rocks and fynbos are pure Atlantic.
intro.body: Bokkoms sits in Bekbaai, a quiet corner of the village where the loudest things are the birds and the waves. Walk to the beach, walk to dinner, and leave the car in the drive.

items.label: Vasco da Gama Monument, St Helena Bay

things.alt: The coastal path through fynbos above the sea
things.title: Walk the coast
things.text: Follow the shoreline into Cape Columbine Nature Reserve, with its lighthouse, granite outcrops and hidden coves.

things.title: Watch the birds
things.text: Gulls, cormorants and oystercatchers work the rocks and the tideline. Bring binoculars.

things.alt: A windsurfer in the surf off Paternoster
things.title: Catch the wind
things.text: The steady West Coast wind makes Paternoster a favourite with windsurfers and kiters.

things.title: Spring flowers
things.text: From late winter into spring the veld around the village turns white, orange and gold with wild flowers.

things.title: Rock pools & photographs
things.text: Clear water, smooth granite and long golden evenings — a gift for photographers.

things.alt: Paintings, ceramics and crafts on show inside The Art Shed gallery in Paternoster
things.title: The Art Shed
things.text: Browse The Art Shed, the Paternoster gallery where Wilko Roon’s work is on show — then wander the white lanes and stop for coffee.

getting.title:
Getting
*here*
getting.text: Paternoster is about 150 km north of Cape Town — roughly two hours by car along the R27 West Coast road, turning off through Vredenburg. Free private parking waits at the door.
